transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

It's really hard for me to talk about, but I've been having these episodes where I eat a massive amount of food in one sitting. I just feel completely out of control, like I can't stop myself once I start.
After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for them by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Or do the episodes happen without those behaviors?
Yes, I try to make up for it by fasting and skipping meals for a long time, or by exercising excessively to burn off the calories. I don't force myself to throw up or use laxatives, though.
What is your current weight and height, and have you recently been at a significantly low weight for your body?
I'm not actually sure of my exact height and weight right now. I don't think I've been at a significantly low weight recently, though.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself or your self-worth?

It honestly affects everything; my self-worth and mood are completely dependent on my weight and shape. If I see even the slightest increase on the scale, I feel absolutely terrible about myself. I constantly obsess over the numbers and find myself checking the scale all the time.
Are you actively trying to keep your weight down by severely restricting what you eat, and do you have an intense fear of gaining weight even if others say you are not overweight?

Yes, I have an intense, constant fear of gaining even a single pound, no matter what anyone else says. To try and control that, I often severely restrict my food intake and go through long periods of fasting to prevent any weight gain.
Even if you’re not sure of the exact numbers, have other people or doctors told you that your weight was dangerously low or much lower than expected for your body?
No, no one has ever told me that my weight is dangerously low. It's never really been brought up as a concern by my family or any doctors.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by recurrent compensatory behaviors including fasting, meal skipping, and excessive exercise. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by weight and shape, and there is no evidence that the patient has been at a significantly low body weight, supporting Bulimia Nervosa over Anorexia Nervosa.
